title: sync script: LLM session residual attack surface beyond the git-state pin (refs/hooks/push/untracked)
description: Reviewer kimi-k3 rounds 2-4 on the d42k git-state pin (sync-beads-workers.sh llm_semantic_merge). The pin closes HEAD/ref/MERGE_HEAD/staged-name mutations. Remaining session-capability residuals, accepted and documented in the pin's block comment, need a design decision (sandbox the session vs accept); none are closable by more pin lines: (1) WORKER-BRANCH REFS: session can 'git update-ref refs/heads/beads-worker-N' or checkout+commit on a worker branch; the loop's clean-merge path (no content gate by design — worker output is trusted) then merges session-authored commits later in the same run. A for-each-ref snapshot compare false-positives on legit concurrent worker commits, so detection needs a trust-model change (e.g. session runs without git write access, or merge-commits get a content review gate). (2) HOOKS/CONFIG PERSISTENCE: session can plant .git/hooks/post-commit or set core.hooksPath/core.fsmonitor; the script runs git status/commit afterwards every branch, giving the session code execution at driver privilege later in the same run, immune to the rewind. (3) PUSH-TO-REMOTE: session pushing an ungated commit puts it on the remote; local rewind then makes divergence harder to notice. (4) UNTRACKED-FILE WEDGE: session plants untracked files at paths a later branch adds, wedging its merge fail-closed (availability only; 'git clean' rejected by repo no-delete posture). (5) UNSTAGED WORKTREE VANDALISM of tracked non-.beads files persists on the SUCCESS path (commit --no-edit is index-only; failure paths clean it, success path doesn't). Related already-filed: 840r (staged content mutation), 0mqr (.beads writes), 7mvj (timeout -k), x79p (path-list word-split).
